newsitem.title: USA: Isolyser sees record Q2 sales of $42.4mln.
newsitem.headline: Isolyser sees record Q2 sales of $42.4mln.

text.p: Isolyser Co Inc said Monday it expected to post record sales of $42.4 million in the second quarter ended June 30, compared with $31.1 million the year before.

The company attributed the results to increased sales in its custom procedural tray business. A company spokesman was not immediately available to comment on how the increased sales would affect the company's bottomline.
A May 9 First Call estimate of two brokers put the company's second quarter earnings at a loss of $0.08 a share.

The company said its second-quarter sales were the highest in its history. It posted a loss of $0.10 a share on sales of $40.0 million in the first quarter, compared with a profit of $0.01 a share on sales of $40.1 million the year before.
Chairman Gene McGrevin said in a statement Isolyser realigned its marketing and sales, which would result in annualized cost savings of $2.5 million.
Isolyser said it is still searching for a chief executive to replace Robert Taylor, who retired May 1. It also said it is looking for a vice president of research and development.
The company's stock traded at 4 Monday morning, up 3/4.
